players.name: Afsar Zazai
players.didyouKnow: His favourite shot is the extra cover drive
players.bio:
Wicketkeeper-batsman Afsar Zazai was just 16 when he was included in the Afghanistan squad for the 2010 ICC Under-19 World Cup in New Zealand.

He represented his country at a second Under-19 World Cup in 2012, this time in Australia, and the 21-year-old will be familiar with the local conditions when he heads to the 2015 ICC Cricket World Cup.

Long seen as a senior prospect for his country, Zazai was impressive in his first-class debut 2012 when he scored an unbeaten 84 in an upset win over Netherlands. 

His first one-day international cap followed in November 2014 against United Arab Emirates, and again Zazai produced an excellent performance first-up. He scored 60, took one catch and pulled off a stumping, following up with 51 in his second ODI.

players.name: Sharafuddin Ashraf
players.didyouKnow: His first ODI wicket was Zimbabwe’s Brendan Taylor.
players.bio:
A newcomer to the Afghanistan team, Sharafuddin Ashraf made his first international appearance against Zimbabwe in July 2015.

The left-arm spinner picked up six wickets in his first five outings, including an impressive 3-29 against Zimbabwe in his fourth match.

He travelled to Australia and New Zealand for the ICC Cricket World Cup 2015 warm-up tour in September 2014, where he was particularly impressive against a Western Australia XI, collecting 3-33.

players.name: KL Rahul
players.didyouKnow: He enjoys rock climbing in his spare time.
players.bio:
A regular in the India top order for the best part of a decade, KL Rahul has made international centuries in all three formats.

Having made his Test debut during the 2014 Boxing Day Test, Rahul took a bit of time to find his feet at the top level. In 2016 he averaged 59.88 for the calendar year, which included his special 199 against England in Chennai.

Although an accomplished wicketkeeper, his opportunity to keep wickets for India have been rare given their strength in that field during his career.

Known for his elegant stroke play, Rahul has also proven himself to be a team man, moving up and down the batting order to accommodate his side’s needs.

He has been one of the most prolific run-scorer in the IPL. The tournament has also given him the chance to display his leadership skills, having led the Punjab Kings and the Lucknow Superchargers in the past. Rahul has also been part of the Indian leadership group and has led the team in all three formats.

players.name: Yashasvi Jaiswal
players.bio:
A dashing left-handed batter, Yashasvi Jaiswal was identified as a future talent from a young age and moved to Mumbai as a 12-year-old to chase his cricket dream.

He was the player of the tournament at the Under-19 World Cup in 2020 as India finished runners up.

Jaiswal would then have a few seasons with Rajasthan Royals, going in and out of the team as he established himself, before becoming a force in the 2023 edition of the IPL. He finished with the fifth-most runs (625), scored a maiden century (124) and belted the fastest fifty in the tournament's history, off only 13 balls against KKR.

That led to a Test and T20I debut months later, with his adaptation to Test cricket being especially smooth.

Jaiswal scored 171 in his first outing against West Indies as a 21-year-old, and scored two double centuries against England in the same series in early 2024.

players.name: Shubman Gill
players.bio:
Easy on the eye and effortlessly talented, Shubman Gill was named vice-captain for India's campaign at the 2018 Under-19 World Cup.

He made his ODI debut just a year later, and a year after that was making his Test debut against Australia in the Boxing Day Test. Gill applied himself impressively in the final three Tests of that famous 2020-21 series, which saw the Indians win Down Under again against the odds.

That being said, it took time for results to come at Test level and he was given time to succeed, with his first century coming in his 23rd innings.

Once he regained his spot in the ODI in 2022, Gill's form in the 50-over format has been incredible, highlight by his 208 against New Zealand in 2023.

Gill scored the most runs in IPL 2023 (890) and had a strong ODI World Cup later that year, part of the India XI that ultimately lost to Australia in the final in Ahmedabad.

The "Prince" of Indian cricket was handed over the reins of the country's Test and ODI sides in 2025.

players.name: Rishabh Pant
players.bio:
A swashbuckling batter who plays in a seemingly care-free style, Rishabh Pant made his Test debut in England as a 21-year-old, but he’d already been making waves well before that.

He rose to prominence at the 2016 Under-19 World Cup, scoring a century against Namibia and an 18-ball fifty against Nepal. By 19, he had a first-class triple century and an IPL contract.

So an international career seemed imminent, and by his third Test at the Oval (114 from 146 balls) he’d already notched his first hundred.

Fast-forward a few months and Pant played a major hand in India’s maiden Border-Gavaskar Trophy victory in Australia, including a blistering 159 not out in Sydney.

However, perhaps Pant’s most iconic knock came two seasons later, when he returned to Australia and flourished once again.

Left out for the 2020-21 series opener in Adelaide, Pant returned to the XI and after a 97 in Sydney guided India to a stunning final-day victory in Brisbane with his instantly classic 89 not out.

In December 2022, Pant’s world was rocked when he was involved in a serious car crash and was lucky to survive.

His comeback to cricket came in the 2024 IPL and he was back in the Test team by September, making a century against Bangladesh on return.

players.name: Dhruv Jurel
players.bio:
Dhruv Jurel is an exciting right-handed wicketkeeper who was India's vice-captain for the 2020 Under-19 World Cup in South Africa.

Jurel's maiden first-class century, in just his sixth match, was a mammoth 249 for Uttar Pradesh in the Ranji Trophy.

Jurel played his first three Test matches against England in the bumper five-match series in early 2024, with Rishabh Pant unavailable.

players.name: Washington Sundar
players.bio:
Hailing from Chennai in India’s south, Washington Sundar featured as a batting allrounder in the 2016 Under-19 World Cup as a 16-year-old.

The following year, Sundar made his IPL debut for Rising Pune Super Giants and his economical off-spin caught the eye.

By the end of 2017, his fast-tracked rise was complete, making his ODI and T20I debuts against Sri Lanka.

A really strong performance for Royal Challengers Bangalore in the 2020 IPL, where his economy rate was only 5.96 across 15 matches, helped earn him a call up to India’s Test squad that travelled to Australia at the end of the year.

Injury to fellow Tamil Nadu spinner Ravichandran Ashwin allow Sundar to make his Test debut in Brisbane in early 2021, a famous match where India chased a big fourth-innings total to secure the Border-Gavaskar Trophy.

Although he was consistently around the national T20 squad from 2019 onwards, Sundar was overlooked for the 20-over World Cups in 2021, 2022 and 2024.

The offie ended a three-and-a-half year absence from the Test team with his 7-59 against New Zealand in October 2024.

players.name: Kuldeep Yadav
players.bio:
Kuldeep Yadav made his international debut in a Test match against Australia at Dharamsala in March 2017. He took 4-68 in the first-innings. His ODI debut followed in June 2017, while his T20I debut was in July.

Idolising the great Shane Warne, the left-arm wrist spinner caused plenty of trouble to batters with low speeds and a high degree of turn early in his career.

In December 2019, Kuldeep became the first Indian bowler to claim two international hat-tricks. He achieved the feat in an ODI against the West Indies. His first had come against in Australia at the Eden Gardens in 2017, also in an ODI fixture. Kuldeep had also recorded a hat-trick in the 2014 U19 World Cup.

However, he entered a difficult period in 2019, when his formed dipped and stats took a hit.

Kuldeep made a strong comeback after a knee surgery in 2021, with new variations also added to his arsenal.

Kuldeep has spent a large part of his Test career on the bench, staying behind Ravichandran Ashwin and Ravindra Jadeja in the pecking order. However, he has been amongst the wickets whenever he has been given the opportunity in the longest format.

He was part of the dominant Indian white-ball teams that won the 2024 T20 World Cup and the 2025 Champions Trophy.

players.name: Mohammed Siraj
players.bio:
A late bloomer who only picked up cricket as a teenager, Mohammad Siraj is a fiery fast bowler from Hyderabad in the centre of India.

Siraj burst onto the scene at Sunrise’s Hyderabad under the leadership of David Warner, and quickly bowled his way into international calculations.

His ODI debut came in Adelaide in 2019 in a win over Australia, two years after his first appearance in T20 internationals.

Two summers later though, during Australia’s 2020-21 season, Siraj really made his mark on the global stage.

After a Test debut in the Boxing Day Test, Siraj claimed five wickets in the second innings of India’s historic Test victory at the Gabba in Brisbane.

Although inconsistent, the right-armer is capable of the truly brilliant, showcased by his one-day 6-21 against Sri Lanka in the lead up to the 2023 World Cup, and his 6-15 in the first session of the second Test against South Africa in early 2024.

players.name: Prasidh Krishna
players.bio:
Prasidh Krishna made his international debut for India in an ODI against England in 2021. Recording figures of 4 for 54, he became the first Indian bowler to claim a 4-wicket-haul on ODI debut.

His Test and T20Is debuts followed in 2023.

With his shining first-class and List A performances for Karnataka, Prasidh came to be regarded as one of the most promising young quicks in India.

He made his first-class debut for his state side against a Bangladesh A team in 2017 and took a five-for. That performance earned the then 19-year-old a call-up to MRF Pace Academy in Chennai where he was coached by Australian fast-bowling legend Glenn McGrath.

In 2019, Prasidh was invited to train under Jeff Thomson at Cricket Australia's Centre of Excellence. These experiences played a significant role in his growth as a fast bowler.

While his career has been marred by injuries that have not allowed him to establish a regular place in the Indian sides, he was been part of some significant tours for his country.

Prasidh got to play a home World Cup when he was added to India's 2023 Cricket World Cup squad as a replacement for injured allrounder Hardik Pandya.

During the 2024-25 Border-Gavaskar Trophy series, he came into the Indian side in the Sydney Test in place of Jasprit Bumrah and took six Australian wickets. Later in the same year, he played three Tests on India's tour of England.
